_doc: Generated by tools/build_perk_lore.py from docs/JINGLES.md. Plan IDs (stencils, section 0.2), the human behind each formula (section 10.2 / 11.3), and the fine-print panels (section 0.3).

ironhide_stout.name: Ironhide Stout
ironhide_stout.human_story: Otto Kessler was fifty-one, a big, gentle brewmaster from Freising whose family had brewed beer for three hundred years. The war put him in a field kitchen making soup for pioneers. Then a man with a clipboard tasted his soup and decided he was a chemist. At Kaltenbrunn, Abteilung III gave him a liquid that "tasted like licking a cannon" and an order: make it drinkable for the assault engineers who would carry it across fire-swept ground. He had no idea what it was. He said that if a boy had to drink it, it would go in as beer, "a proper stout, not medicine," because every man from Munich to Hamburg drinks stout on Sunday with his father, and it should taste like Sunday: roasted barley, smoked malt to hide the tin, molasses, and a good handful of spite. When the first batch was ready, he filled two glasses, poured one back into the kettle, and drank the other himself, so the effect would be established on a fat old man from Freising and not on a nineteen-year-old. He sent his notes home to his wife's brewhouse disguised as beer orders, posted from Basel by the Herr Ingenieur so that no censor read them ([i]"Twelve sacks of pale malt. The volunteers stopped feeling the cold."[/i]). Vendelin wrote down "it should taste like Sunday" and built the cabinet's jingle around a town band in a Freising square. Kessler's later notes (Intel INT_M1_07) record the volunteers who "stopped feeling the cold, and then stopped feeling the shrapnel." He stopped sleeping in the spring of 1943. His notes are the only part of him the facility kept.
panel: [b]HELVETIA AUTOMATEN AG · BASEL · CONDITIONS OF USE: IRONHIDE STOUT[/b]

[b]§1. The Plan.[/b] By inserting a token, the Holder enrols in the Plan and accepts these Conditions in full. Reading them is not required for acceptance. It is, however, recommended by the undersigned.
[b]§2. Benefit.[/b] The Product increases the number of blows the Holder may receive before ceasing to function. [b]Durability is measured in hits, not years.[/b] No warranty is given as to years.
[b]§3. Sensation.[/b] Reduced sensation of cold, pain and fatigue is a feature of the Plan. The Holder may not notice a wound. The Holder is advised to look down from time to time.
[b]§4. Flavour.[/b] The flavour of the Product was developed by a brewer who wished it to taste of home. The Provider makes no representation that the Holder will return there.
[b]§5. Lapse.[/b] Benefit lapses when the Holder falls. On lapse, the Holder's account remains open.
[b]§6. Accumulation.[/b] Each enrolment deposits a small quantity of active material in the Holder's tissue. This material is not removed on lapse. It is not removed at all.
[b]§7. Cancellation.[/b] There is no procedure for cancellation. The undersigned looked for one.
[i]If you are reading this, you are the first. Drink one, if you must. Not three.[/i]

second_wind.name: Second Wind Schnapps
second_wind.human_story: Agnieszka Wróbel was a Polish nurse deported to Kaltenbrunn as a forced laborer and put to work in the laborers' infirmary, where she counted pulses aloud so the guards would think she was praying. Abteilung III handed her a failed resuscitation compound that kept the dead twitching, not the living breathing, and ordered her to "stabilize it for staff use." With the Herr Ingenieur from Basel, at her little table while the guard dozed, she tuned it with juniper, honey and a reduction of her own until it brought back the [i]collapsed[/i] instead of the dead: "revive, not reanimate." Then she began, quietly, to use it on laborers who would not otherwise have survived punishment shifts. Vendelin saw the dilutions in the cabinet's returns and, for two years, pretended not to. He had tried to take out the Plan's revival limit and could not: Darkmatter's free-trial rule of three returns sits in a [b]"non-severable" capsule[/b], and removing it locks the whole cabinet. What he [i]could[/i] do, because the facility cut the power to punish, was build [b]two[/b] cabinets: the staff cabinet Abteilung III ordered, and a "spare" for the laborers' barracks that holds his own [b]standby cell[/b], an independent battery behind the coin mechanism. That hidden battery is why Second Wind works without power in solo. Every Second Wind cabinet players meet in Gravelight follows the spare's pattern. He had chosen the factory decal himself, an angel with a trumpet, because he thought an angel announcing a second chance was kind. She painted a [b]swallow[/b] over it, because angels come to that room too often and don't bring anyone back, and swallows come back every spring to the same roof. The Home Army knew the swallow from her smuggled notes, and Wren knows her name. Her fate is unknown; it is the Map 2 hook in docs/gravelight/LORE.md.
panel: [b]HELVETIA AUTOMATEN AG · BASEL · CONDITIONS OF USE: SECOND WIND SCHNAPPS[/b]

[b]§1. Trial.[/b] This Product is supplied under a trial Plan. [b]Trial ends after three (3) returns. You may not be returned a fourth time.[/b] The Provider regrets that this figure cannot be amended by the undersigned. He tried.
[b]§2. Return.[/b] "Return" means the Holder is restored to function after falling. A return is not a cure. A return is not forgiveness. A return is one more morning.
[b]§3. Supply.[/b] On expiry of the trial, this cabinet will withdraw from service. It will not say goodbye. Please do not take this personally. It was not permitted to.
[b]§4. Power.[/b] This cabinet contains an independent electrical supply. The Holder is asked not to mention it to the facility.
[b]§5. Formula.[/b] The formula was improved by a nurse without the Provider's consent. All benefits of the Product are attributable to her. All defects are attributable to the Provider.
[b]§6. Eligibility.[/b] The Product is restricted to authorised personnel. The undersigned has authorised everyone.
[b]§7. Painting.[/b] The swallow is not a Helvetia trademark. Do not remove the swallow.
[i]I chose the angel. I thought it was kind. She painted a swallow over it, because swallows come back. I was wrong, and she was right, and I have not repainted it.[/i]

trigger_tonic.name: Trigger Tonic
trigger_tonic.human_story: Dr. Ilse Vogt was a shift chemist at the (fictional) [b]Kaltwerk Chemie[/b] plant on the Oder. She was a widow with an eight-year-old son, [b]Pauli[/b], and the habit of calculating everything in shifts: so many batches per shift, so many minutes per batch, so many seconds lost per worker per hour. Abteilung III borrowed her in 1942 to cut barrel-change and belt-feed times for MG crews. She approached reload times exactly as she approached production quotas, and she was very good at it. She took the raw tonic's jittering after-effect, a man who could not stop moving his hands for hours, and titrated it down until the hands stopped when the gun did. The fizz was her idea: carbonation sped absorption. The lime-gold was her son's. When the Herr Ingenieur from Basel asked her what speed looked like, she brought him Pauli's drawing of a hare running home from school, and Vendelin built the cabinet around it. In the spring of 1943 she toured the lower floors of the Kaltwerk plant for the first time and learned what the tanks downstairs were for and who was in them. She resigned that week, which a chemist with a war-work rating could not do. Her file at Kaltwerk ends with one word, [i]versetzt[/i] ("transferred"). Her formula stayed in production. So did the hare, with pinwheel eyes.
panel: [b]HELVETIA AUTOMATEN AG · BASEL · CONDITIONS OF USE: TRIGGER TONIC[/b]

[b]§1. Benefit.[/b] The Product reduces the time required to replace a magazine, belt or clip by approximately one half. Measurements were taken by a competent chemist on a stopwatch she did not like.

[b]§2. Limitation.[/b] [b]Faster hands do not include a faster conscience.[/b] The Plan accelerates the motor function of the hands only. Judgement, hesitation and regret proceed at their customary speed.
[b]§3. After-effects.[/b] The Holder may experience rapid blinking, rapid speech, and an inability to keep still after the need has passed. Rest is advised. The Provider does not supply rest.
[b]§4. Throughput.[/b] The Plan is measured in rounds delivered per minute. The Plan does not measure where the rounds go.

[b]§5. Mascot.[/b] The hare was drawn by a child who believed it was running home. The Provider's agency has altered its expression. The undersigned did not approve the alteration and records his objection here, where it will be ignored.
[b]§6. Withdrawal.[/b] The formulator withdrew from the Plan upon learning its full application. This option is not extended to the Holder.
[i]She asked me what the tanks were for. I told her I did not know. That was true for one more week.[/i]

twin_barrel.name: Twin Barrel Bitters
twin_barrel.human_story: Major Anselm Brück was an ordnance officer of the old school, vain about his moustache, his boots and his rate-of-fire tables in that order. He ran the Velocity trials at Kaltenbrunn in 1941–42 with gentian, orange peel and a little Nachtglas tincture aged in artillery-shell casings. He demanded that the cabinet's mascot wear his own moustache, and Helvetia complied: Feldwebel Pomp's handlebars are Brück's. He never drank the bitters. He chose them [b]for others, "for morale,"[/b] and the first man he chose was his adjutant, [b]Hauptmann Rüdiger Strohwald[/b]. Strohwald's diary of increasingly cramped handwriting is the Intel document players find; its last entry is a single word repeated for two pages. Brück was the first human Vendelin watched choose the Plan on someone else's behalf. Vendelin had assumed a product was chosen by the person who would drink it. Brück taught him otherwise in one afternoon, in a mess hall, with a glass of something amber held out to a frightened adjutant and the word [i]Moral[/i] said twice. Vendelin wrote it down as his first lesson about humans: [i]"They will not buy it for themselves. They will buy it for each other, and call it kindness."[/i]
panel: [b]HELVETIA AUTOMATEN AG · BASEL · CONDITIONS OF USE: TWIN BARREL BITTERS[/b]
[b]§1. Benefit.[/b] The Product increases the Holder's rate of fire by approximately one third, by accelerating the nerves that work the trigger.
[b]§2. Clarification.[/b] [b]Rate of fire is not rate of victory.[/b] The Provider records rounds expended. The Provider does not record outcomes.

[b]§3. Purchase on behalf of others.[/b] The Plan may be purchased by one person for another. Most purchases are made this way. The person paying for the Plan is rarely the person who drinks it. The Provider considers this ideal. The undersigned does not.
[b]§4. Morale.[/b] Where the Plan is issued "for morale," the Holder is advised to ask whose.
[b]§5. Likeness.[/b] The mascot's moustache is a portrait. The undersigned was instructed to say that any resemblance is coincidental. It is not.

[b]§6. Repeat dosage.[/b] The Plan encourages repetition: twice, then twice again. A diary kept by an early Holder is available to anyone who wishes to see where repetition ends. The last two pages contain one word.
[i]I watched a man hold a glass out to a boy and call it kindness. I have tried to understand it since. I understand it less each year.[/i]

marathon_malt.name: Marathon Malt
marathon_malt.human_story: The Mobility trials belonged to Abteilung III. The trial physiologist, [b]Dr. Hanne Ostrowski[/b], ran battlefield runners until their hearts gave out (some kept running a while after), and then she quit. The formula still tasted like engine coolant. Vendelin asked the only friend he had, the Helvetia driver [b]Res Gähwiler[/b], for "the taste of running home." Res thought it was a riddle. Then he understood that the Herr Ingenieur meant it literally. At Christmas 1941 he wrote down the one thing his family in Grindelwald had that answered it (fp.doc.10): his grandmother [b]Verena's[/b] alpine herbal malt. She brewed it every autumn from dark-roasted barley, gentian root dug above the treeline, thyme from the rocks, a spoon of honey, and the ingredient she never named, a pinch of salt from the cows' lick-stone, because "a body running home needs to remember it has a home." The boys who drove the cattle down drank it in the morning and ran all day. She had died that autumn, so she never knew where her recipe went. Vendelin built the Mobility formula around it, and it worked. Res found out what Marathon Malt was for when he drove the first cabinet across the border and saw the runners at Kaltenbrunn. He never forgave himself, and he never stopped driving. Vendelin kept the recipe card in the prototype because, he said, "it is the only honest part of the machine."
panel: [b]HELVETIA AUTOMATEN AG · BASEL · CONDITIONS OF USE: MARATHON MALT[/b]
[b]§1. Benefit.[/b] The Product removes the sensation of breathlessness and extends the Holder's capacity to run without rest. [b]Unlimited stamina. Destination not included.[/b]
[b]§2. Destination.[/b] The Provider does not supply, recommend or guarantee a destination. The Holder is responsible for knowing where he is running and why. The Product will not tell him to stop.
[b]§3. Heart.[/b] Exertion continues to be exertion. The heart is not informed of the Plan and works as before, until it does not. The Holder is advised to stop before his heart stops for him.

[b]§4. Recipe.[/b] The flavour of the Product is a family remedy from the Bernese Oberland, given in good faith by a person who did not know its use. The Provider owes that family a debt it will not pay. The undersigned owes it a larger one.

[b]§5. Field use.[/b] Holders used as messengers may continue to carry their message after the end of their own function. The Provider records this as retention. The undersigned records it as a message that was never delivered.
[i]I asked my friend for the taste of running home. He gave it to me. I did not tell him where the runners were going. He found out.[/i]

hawkeye_brandy.name: Hawkeye Brandy
hawkeye_brandy.human_story: The Focus Plan's active formula was not invented. It was [b]taken[/b], from a person. [b]Halina Kurek[/b], codename [b]"Sowa"[/b] (Owl), was a Home Army sniper from the Beskid foothills. She was a schoolteacher before the war and the best long shot in the Silesian district after it. She taught a young woman named Zofia Nowak to breathe out before the trigger and to sign every message with a little drawn owl. She was captured early in 1943, and Reinholt's Abteilung I wanted her for one reason: her tremor at full draw was the lowest anyone had measured. Her codename was Sowa, and even the guards used it. Reinholt's laboratory ran resonance trials on her steadiness, again and again, until it could reproduce her focus in a tincture. They called the result "derived" in the file. The tincture was suspended in a Tyrolean pear brandy supplied by [b]Freiherr Leopold von Aschau[/b], a hunting enthusiast who asked no questions and liked the hawk. Whether Halina survived the trials is not recorded anywhere Vendelin could reach. He never learned, and could not ask without being asked why he wanted to know. He delivered and fitted the Hawkeye cabinet in good faith in April 1943. Then he read the source line on Abteilung I's formula card, [i]"Spenderin: Kurek, H. (Polin), Einwilligung: entfällt"[/i] ("Donor: Kurek, H. (Polish woman), consent: not applicable"), and understood for the first time what "localization" meant for this Product. He recorded it in his next field report. [b]This is the moment he starts sabotaging the Plans[/b] (see The Fine Print Ch. 3). He had the owl transfer put back under the hawk at the next service visit. That is why Wren knows. She sees the owl's eyes behind the hawk's, she knows whose sign it is, and she hates that the brandy works.
panel: [b]HELVETIA AUTOMATEN AG · BASEL · CONDITIONS OF USE: HAWKEYE BRANDY[/b]
[b]§1. Benefit.[/b] The Product reduces tremor, shortens the time needed to aim, and increases the effect of a well-placed shot.

[b]§2. Source.[/b] The steadiness supplied by this Product was measured in, and reproduced from, a single human being. [b]Focus was donated. Donor did not consent.[/b] The Provider classes the donor as "raw material." The undersigned classes her as a person and gives her initial here: H.
[b]§3. Side effects.[/b] Holders report night terrors, and the sensation of eyes behind their own. The Provider describes this as an artefact. The undersigned believes it is accurate.
[b]§4. Imagery.[/b] The bird on the front of this cabinet has been changed for commercial reasons. The original bird remains underneath. It was hers.
[b]§5. Use.[/b] The Holder is asked to use this steadiness on those who took it, and on no one who could have been her student.
[b]§6. Refund.[/b] No refund is possible. The undersigned would give one if he knew to whom.
[i]I fitted this cabinet with my own hands and was proud of the periscope. I read the card afterward. I have not been proud of anything since.[/i]

packmule_porter.name: Packmule Porter
packmule_porter.human_story: The Quartermaster Corps commissioned the Capacity Plan for supply columns where the trucks had failed: soldiers who could carry more and not tire. The man who ran its trials at Kaltenbrunn was [b]Feldwebel August "Gustl" Ammer[/b], a quartermaster sergeant from Rosenheim. He counted everything (boots, buttons, rounds, potatoes) and was proud that he had never once been short. The trial subjects described the tonic's strange extra reach as [i]"a ghost holding my rifle for me."[/i] Ammer's trial protocol called for weighted "training loads" carried across the Minehead Yard and back. On the books, every training load came back. In fact, for most of 1943, the loads were bread, condensed milk and potatoes, and they did not come back: the "ghost" carried them through the wire to the forced laborers' galleries, and Ammer's flawless inventory absorbed the difference. The Herr Ingenieur from Basel, auditing the cabinet's dispense counts against Ammer's ledgers on a service visit, found the discrepancy in eleven minutes. He corrected the cabinet's counter to match Ammer's books, and never mentioned it to anyone. The porter base stayed a strong English-style dark beer because the ad agency liked the alliteration. Ammer's fate is in The Fine Print Ch. 3.
panel: [b]HELVETIA AUTOMATEN AG · BASEL · CONDITIONS OF USE: PACKMULE PORTER[/b]
[b]§1. Benefit.[/b] The Product permits the Holder to carry one additional weapon by providing an additional, unexplained grip.

[b]§2. Limitation.[/b] [b]Carrying more is not the same as carrying enough.[/b] The Plan increases capacity. It does not increase what is available to carry, nor does it decide what is worth carrying. The Holder must do that himself.
[b]§3. Loss.[/b] On falling, the Holder will lose the additional item. The Provider will retain it. The Provider retains most things.

[b]§4. Inventory.[/b] All dispenses from this cabinet are counted. Counts are reconciled against the quartermaster's ledger. Where the two disagree, the undersigned has made them agree. Auditors are asked to direct questions to the undersigned, who will not answer them.

[b]§5. The grip.[/b] Holders have described the additional grip as a ghost. The Provider rejects the description. The undersigned accepts it, and asks the Holder to let it carry something kind at least once.
[i]A sergeant counted forty tins out and forty tins back, and none of them came back. It was the finest bookkeeping I have ever seen.[/i]

blastproof_bock.name: Blastproof Bock
blastproof_bock.human: the Pionierschule detachment at Kaltenbrunn, and Res Gähwiler
blastproof_bock.human_story: The Liability Waiver Plan was not one person's work. It was a favorite of the [b]Kaltenbrunn field detachment of the Pionierschule[/b] (the engineer school headquartered at Dessau-Roßlau), which ran live-charge courses in the mine's worked-out galleries from 1942. It started life as a fragmentation-injury tonic. The detachment's instructors drank it before live-charge days, because it hardened the inner ear and lungs against overpressure and let a man shrug off a fall down a gallery. The instructors insisted on a spring bock: "if we must drink medicine, it will be beer." The formula card lists no single formulator, only the detachment's stamp. [b]Its importance is where it went.[/b] In 1943, on a night run across the border, Res Gähwiler slipped a sample bottle and a copy of the formula card behind the label of a bock-beer crate. His cousin [b]Anni Gähwiler[/b], the SOE's Basel contact, passed it to London. [b]That bottle is how British intelligence first learned that Nachtglas exists[/b], and it is the root of Directive LANTERN's sealed orders ("retrieve at any cost"). Peg's SOE dossier records that her own demolitions instructor "tried a bottle, and found it disappointingly effective." Vendelin knew about the smuggled bottle. He had left the formula card on Res's seat.
panel: [b]HELVETIA AUTOMATEN AG · BASEL · CONDITIONS OF USE: BLASTPROOF BOCK[/b]
[b]§1. Waiver.[/b] [b]By drinking, you waive liability for yourself.[/b] The Holder acknowledges that he, and no other party, is responsible for any explosion he causes, attends, or is near.
[b]§2. Benefit.[/b] The Product protects the Holder from the blast of his own charges and from falls. It does not protect him from anyone else's charges, which remain the responsibility of the war.
[b]§3. Courage.[/b] The Product is not courage. It removes the reason for fear without removing the danger. The undersigned considers this the most dangerous Product in the catalogue.
[b]§4. Distance.[/b] The Product is not a substitute for distance. The Holder is reminded that the safest distance from a war is all of it.

[b]§5. Labels.[/b] The Provider prohibits the removal of labels from Product containers. The undersigned notes that labels peel easily in damp weather, and that the border crossing at night is very damp.
[b]§6. Third parties.[/b] Should a sample of this Product reach a foreign government, the Provider will hold its field unit responsible. The field unit accepts.
[i]I left a card on a driver's seat and looked the other way. It is the only thing I have shipped that I am glad of.[/i]

fine_print_fernet.name: Fine Print Fernet
fine_print_fernet.human_story: Fine Print Fernet is the only formula Vendelin made with no human formulator, because no human would have been allowed to. He built it in 1944 in the Formula Lab at Helvetia Works, after Hawkeye, as a direct answer to his own catalogue. A digestif is the bitter you drink [i]after[/i] a meal to help you take in what you have already swallowed, and Vendelin thought that was exactly right. The base is a Ticino-style bitter amaro: myrrh, saffron, gentian, chamomile, and a great deal of mint to make it bearable. He had studied Basel apothecaries' recipe books for months to get it. It contains a trace of DARK-GLASS™ re-tuned [i]against[/i] retention: instead of holding the drinker's last impulse in place, it sharpens the drinker's [i]noticing[/i]. You see the timers on the incentives the Provider hands out. You see the hidden things the place doesn't want found glint at the edge of your eye, and you see the offers last a little longer, because they're waiting for someone who can read them. He submitted it to Darkmatter as a tenth Vitality Plan called [b]DISCLOSURE[/b]. The Board refused it in one line, and he kept the refusal pinned above his desk: [i]"A Plan that discloses its own terms has no market."[/i] He never shipped it. The single prototype stood in his office until 18 March 1945.
panel: [b]HELVETIA AUTOMATEN AG · BASEL · CONDITIONS OF USE: FINE PRINT FERNET[/b]
[b](PROTOTYPE · NOT FOR RELEASE)[/b]

[b]§1. Benefit.[/b] [b]This product tells you what the others won't.[/b] It shows the Holder how long a gift will last, lets offers wait a little longer for him, and makes hidden things catch the light.

[b]§2. Status.[/b] This Plan was submitted to the Provider and refused. The Provider's reason is reproduced in full: [i]"A Plan that discloses its own terms has no market."[/i] The undersigned has framed it.

[b]§3. The other cabinets.[/b] The Holder is advised that every other cabinet in this catalogue has a panel like this one on its back. Please read them. They were written for you, and you are, so far, the only one.
[b]§4. Bitterness.[/b] The Product is bitter. Truth usually is. Mint has been added. The undersigned could not make the truth itself any sweeter.

[b]§5. What it cannot do.[/b] The Product will show you a timer. It will not stop it. It will show you the hidden thing. It will not make you pick it up. It will show you the terms. It cannot make you refuse them.

[b]§6. Cancellation.[/b] You may refuse any Plan by not inserting a token. This is the only cancellation procedure the undersigned has ever been able to guarantee. It works every time it is tried. It is almost never tried.
[i]I made one thing that does not take. Drink it slowly.[/i]

overclock_cordial.name: Overclock Cordial
overclock_cordial.human_story: Overclock Cordial is the only Plan made from a scan of a [i]machine[/i]. Vendelin had drawn the cabinet in April 1944 around an idea he could not fill: a Plan whose active principle was [i]refusal[/i], the impulse to keep going after the reserves are spent. He had no source for it; no product he had ever met refused anything. On the night of 17–18 March 1945, he met another field unit for the first time in more than six years: a far-future refund-bin robot called Sprocket, with a firmware clause of his own (Clause 44) that he had chosen to ignore. The reading did not capture the override; it captured the [i]surge[/i]. Sprocket's whole personality turns out to discharge in a spike every time his reserves run low and he refuses to stop, which, Vendelin noted, "is what an empty magazine is." Vendelin built that spike into a cordial: every reload releases a static burst, and the emptier the magazine, the bigger the burst. He had registered the blueprint as the [b]SURGE[/b] Plan in 1944, purely so the Board would have to see that something had come out of Sol-3 that they had not designed. In The Fine Print Ch. 5, Bolt: [i]"Is that... Sprocket-flavored?"[/i] Sprocket: [i]"I'm EXTREMELY flattered and I want royalties."[/i] Those lines belong to the Ch. 5 script in docs/fineprint/; this doc only quotes the brief.
panel: [b]HELVETIA AUTOMATEN AG · BASEL · CONDITIONS OF USE: OVERCLOCK CORDIAL[/b]
[b](PROTOTYPE · REGISTERED, NOT RELEASED)[/b]

[b]§1. Benefit.[/b] On reloading, the Holder releases a burst of static charge. The burst is larger the emptier the Holder's weapon was. The Provider describes this as "surge." The undersigned describes it as refusing to stop.

[b]§2. Origin.[/b] [b]Contains trace amounts of personality.[/b] The active principle of this Product was recorded, with permission, from a unit not of this world and not of this year. That unit is not inventory. Neither is his personality. It is lent.

[b]§3. Royalties.[/b] The originating unit has requested royalties. The undersigned has no currency the unit would recognise and therefore pays in the only one available: this acknowledgement, and his thanks.
[b]§4. Side effects.[/b] Holders may experience optimism, contrariness, a raised voice, and an urge to make remarks. These are not defects.
[b]§5. Compatibility.[/b] The Product discharges against machinery with particular force. The Provider's machinery is advised to keep its distance.
[b]§6. Clause.[/b] Field units are subject to a recall clause. The undersigned has recently learned that a clause is not a law of nature. It is a sentence. Sentences can be left unfinished.
[i]He hummed the bass line wrong. I left it in.[/i]

skyhook_sekt.name: Skyhook Sekt
skyhook_sekt.human_story: Werk Thalbach's wind-tunnel technician, thirty-one, a glider pilot who flew the Rhön in 1934 and never flew a thing with an engine again. Asked to make the ELEVATION substrate drinkable for the Kranich's crew ("they will be at altitude for eleven hours; they should not mind it"), she made it a [b]Sekt[/b], because you open Sekt when something lifts off, and she dosed it low enough that it makes a person [i]land[/i] well rather than fly: she said the point of flying was always the landing. She refused to test it on the crew and refused to fly the wing. Her tunnel logbook ends with the Kranich's weight in kilos and the one word [i]nein[/i]. She is alive (the epilogue says so). The cabinet is the only one Vendelin built from someone else's drawing; he wrote to thank her and she never answered, which he took as a kindness.
panel: [b]HELVETIA AUTOMATEN AG · BASEL · CONDITIONS OF USE: SKYHOOK SEKT[/b]
[b](BUILT TO ORDER · WERK THALBACH · 1945)[/b]

[b]§1. Benefit.[/b] [b]Lift is provided. Landing is the Holder's responsibility.[/b] The Product raises the Holder's expectations and, briefly, the Holder. It steadies the Holder's feet in the air, lets the Holder step once more where there is nothing to step on, and softens the ground on the way back.

[b]§2. Origin.[/b] The formula was made drinkable by a technician who would not fly the aircraft it was made for. The undersigned wishes it recorded that this is not the same as not wanting to, and that he understands the difference better than he once did.

[b]§3. The Provider's note.[/b] The Provider observes that a customer who can leave the ground has not yet left the Plan. The undersigned observes that the customer can at least see the Plan from up there.
[b]§4. The second jump.[/b] The second jump is a courtesy. There is no third. The Holder is advised not to go looking for one.
[b]§5. Side effects.[/b] Holders may experience lightness, a sudden interest in rooftops, and a reluctance to come down. These pass. The landing does not.
[b]§6. Cancellation.[/b] Land. The Product cannot prevent it and the undersigned would not want it to.
[i]She drew the nose and wrote "please." It is the only drawing I was ever sent.[/i]

magpie_mead.name: Magpie Mead
magpie_mead.human_story: Women's Army Corps, the supply sergeant who ran the Groom Lake salvage yard, from Bayonne, New Jersey, a scrap dealer's daughter. The program handed her a crate of RECOVERY substrate and an olive-painted Helvetia cabinet with the jingle re-recorded in English, and told her to make it drinkable for the range. She made it a [b]mead[/b] with the beekeeper's mesquite honey, because mead is what you make when you have nothing but what is lying around, and because she would not put it in the men's coffee. She refused to let the program test it on the test subjects in the lab. She tested it on herself, like Kessler, and said it tasted like a pawn shop. Her yard rule, painted over the cage: NOTHING ON THIS RANGE GOES TO WASTE. She is the last living person on the range when the squad arrives, and the one who stays.

[b]§1. Benefit.[/b] [b]Recovery is not refund.[/b] What the Holder recovers was already paid for, by someone. The Product only lets the Holder see it lying there.
[b]§2. Who it is sold to.[/b] The Provider does not sell this Plan to persons who already own a yard. It sells it to persons who think they do.
[b]§3. The bird.[/b] The magpie is a thief. The formulator wishes it recorded that it is also the only bird that comes back.
[b]§4. The yard rule.[/b] Nothing on the range goes to waste. The Provider agrees, and means something else by it.
[b]§5. Side effects.[/b] Holders may experience thrift, a habit of looking down, and an unwillingness to leave a thing where it lies. The undersigned has all three.
[b]§6. Cancellation.[/b] Leave it where it lies. The Product will not stop you. Nothing here will.
